Council sets tax rate at $13.96, a 12% hike

Mark Pechenik

August 17, 2026,
8:45 PM
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:23
Instaread

The town’s tax rate for this year is $13.96 per $1,000 valuation on taxable properties in town, an increase of nearly 12 % over last year.

The tax rate, also called the mil rate, was approved unanimously by the Town Council at its Aug. 11 meeting. The $1.44 increase from last year’s rate of $12.52 per $1,000 valuation went into effect July 1, 2026, for the 2027 fiscal year.

For a home valued at $300,000, a property owner can expect to pay $4,188 a year, an annual increase of $432.

The property taxes raised will bring in $21,547,730 to fund school, town and county budgets. About 46% goes to the town, 51% percent to the Marshwood school district, and 3% to the county.

The tax rate set by the town includes an overlay amount of $301,046 to cover potential tax abatements and exemptions that might be granted by the Board of Assessment Review. Any overlay funds not spent during the year go into the town’s undesignated fund.

In other business at the Aug. 11 meeting:

  • The council approved the appointment of Evelina Murphy to the Conservation Commission
  • The council approved the addition of Anthony Palazzetti to the Municipal Procurement Policy Ad Hoc Committee. This committee is charged with reviewing the town’s Purchasing Policy and recommending updates to improve clarity, transparency, efficiency and compliance with federal grant requirements, according to the Town website.
